# Performance

Performance in the context of the [[databasen-for-atrieflimren-i-danmark|Databasen for Atrieflimren i Danmark]] (AFDK) refers to the systematic measurement of healthcare quality for patients diagnosed with [[atrieflimren]] (atrial fibrillation) in [[danmark|Danmark]]. Tracked through a series of clinical indicators ([[indikator-1|Indikator 1]] through [[indikator-8|Indikator 8]]) overseen by the [[afdk-styregruppe|Styregruppen for AFDK]] and the [[regionernes-kliniske-kvalitetsudviklingsprogram|Regionernes Kliniske Kvalitetsudviklingsprogram]], these metrics evaluate everything from the prompt initiation of [[antikoagulationsbehandling]] to long-term monitoring and patient education. The data, spanning annual reports from 2023 to 2025, reveals a healthcare system that excels in acute pharmacological interventions but struggles with consistent diagnostic workups and structured patient education.

## Prompt and Long-Term Anticoagulation
A primary measure of performance is the rapid initiation of oral anticoagulation for newly diagnosed patients with a [[cha2ds2-vasc|CHA2DS2-VASc]] score ≥2. National performance for [[indikator-1|Indikator 1]] has consistently met or exceeded the [[standard-90-percent|Standard: ≥90 %]] across the 2023, 2024, and 2025 reporting periods, with rates stabilizing around 91.6% to 92% [^src2] [^src6] [^src10]. At the regional level, [[region-nordjylland|Region Nordjylland]] and [[region-midtjylland|Region Midtjylland]] frequently lead in target fulfillment [^src6] [^src10]. Long-term adherence to treatment ([[indikator-4a|Indikator 4a]]) shows that roughly 88% to 90% of patients remain on anticoagulation one to two years post-diagnosis, though [[region-nordjylland|Region Nordjylland]] is often the only region to consistently meet long-term development goals [^src13] [^src17]. Notably, about 55% to 56% of patients had already redeemed an anticoagulation prescription within 120 days prior to their formal hospital diagnosis, indicating significant pre-hospital or primary care management [^src6] [^src10].

## Diagnostic Workup: Echocardiography and TSH
Performance in diagnostic workup presents a mixed picture. For [[indikator-2|Indikator 2]], the national rate of patients receiving an [[ekkokardiografi|Ekkokardiografi]] within the designated window reached 81.0% in the 2025 report, with [[region-syddanmark|Region Syddanmark]] and [[region-midtjylland|Region Midtjylland]] achieving their development goals [^src11]. However, measuring [[thyreoideastimulerende-hormon-tsh|thyreoideastimulerende hormon (TSH)]] ([[indikator-3|Indikator 3]]) remains a persistent national shortfall. National fulfillment hovers around 76% to 83%, failing to meet the required standards [^src7] [^src12] [^src18]. While [[region-midtjylland|Region Midtjylland]] and the [[horsensklyngen|Horsensklyngen]] consistently post the highest regional and cluster-level TSH testing rates, [[sundhedsklynge-soenderjylland|Sundhedsklynge Sønderjylland]] records drastically lower performance, dropping to 41.2% in one reporting period [^src7] [^src12].

## Safety, Monitoring, and Complications
For patients on [[doac|DOAC]] (Direct Oral Anticoagulants), annual monitoring of renal function via p-creatinin ([[indikator-4b|Indikator 4b]]) is critical. Nationally, about 93.9% to 94.3% of the prevalent population receives this monitoring, narrowly missing the strict ≥95% standard [^src9] [^src14] [^src18]. [[region-nordjylland|Region Nordjylland]] stands out as the only region to consistently fulfill this standard, with all its health clusters meeting the target, whereas eastern Danish regions fail entirely at the cluster level [^src9] [^src19]. Regarding severe complications, the incidence of ischemic stroke ([[indikator-5|Indikator 5]]) among prevalent patients remains low (around 0.8%), allowing the national standard of ≤0.8% to be met in most reports, though [[region-hovedstaden|Region Hovedstaden]] and [[region-sjaelland|Region Sjælland]] occasionally exceed the threshold [^src9] [^src19] [^src20]. [[indikator-7|Indikator 7]] (national incidence 2.1%) also meets its standards nationally and across all regions [^src4] [^src18].

## Patient Education
The most significant performance deficit lies in structured patient education. [[indikator-8|Indikator 8]] tracks whether newly diagnosed patients receive structured education within their first year. National fulfillment is starkly low, measured at just 15.9% to 35% across different reporting periods, falling far short of the 50% minimum standard [^src5] [^src15] [^src18]. Regional variations are vast, ranging from 4.3% to 43%, and no region successfully meets the standard, highlighting a systemic gap in non-pharmacological patient support [^src5] [^src15].
